items.headline: Brewers claw back from 4-0 down — and now lead the Series 2-0
items.body: Milwaukee spotted Tampa Bay a four-run first inning, then roared back to win 5-4 behind Sal Frelick's game-tying homer and a clutch bullpen. The Brewers head to Florida up 2-0, two wins from the franchise's first-ever title.
items.say: How about the Brewers erasing a 4-0 hole in Game 2? Tampa's in real trouble now, down 0-2.

items.headline: Valkyries refuse to die — Golden State evens the Finals 2-2
items.body: A night after Atlanta had a chance to close it out, the expansion Golden State Valkyries gutted out a 67-62 road win, with Gabby Williams scoring 17 and the defense holding Angel Reese to eight points. It's down to a Game 5 (at least) back in the Bay.
items.say: The Valkyries just forced a Game 5 in the Finals — not bad for a team that didn't exist last season.

items.headline: Villa stun City — Nicolás Jackson's double downs the champions
items.body: Aston Villa came from behind at Villa Park to beat Manchester City 2-1, with Nicolás Jackson scoring twice after Erling Haaland had put City in front. A statement result that shakes up the top of the table.
items.say: Did you catch Villa beating Man City? Jackson scored twice — City suddenly look very beatable.

items.headline: DK pull off the 'Elder flip' to stun T1 at Worlds
items.body: Day 2 of the Worlds Swiss stage in Texas gave us the moment of the tournament so far: Dplus KIA stole the Elder Dragon and instantly wiped four-time champs T1 to finish the game and move to 2-0. T1 have work to do to advance.
items.say: You've gotta see the 'Elder flip' DK hit on T1 at Worlds — the whole arena lost it.

items.headline: Allez! The NFL plays its first-ever game in Paris today
items.body: The Steelers and Saints are kicking off the league's first regular-season game at the Stade de France. Early on, Aaron Rodgers passed Peyton Manning for third on the NFL's all-time passing-touchdown list.
items.say: The NFL's in Paris for the first time ever today — Steelers and Saints at the Stade de France.

items.headline: 'Clayface' oozes to No. 1 — and lands a rare A- for a horror movie
items.body: DC's body-horror swing won the weekend with an estimated $24M opening and a surprising A- CinemaScore, a grade scary movies almost never get. A24's 'You Can See Everything' held second around $20M.
items.say: 'Clayface' actually topped the box office — and horror fans say it's genuinely great, not just gross.

items.headline: Everyone's hiding behind the couch for Netflix's 'Below'
items.body: The creature-feature thriller starring Josh Hartnett and Charlie Heaton — a sea monster terrorizing a remote Newfoundland town — is parked at No. 1 on Netflix for a second straight week. A pretty perfect spooky-season binge.
items.say: Have you started 'Below' on Netflix? It's the creepy sea-monster show everyone's bingeing before Halloween.

items.headline: Drake and Don Toliver are everywhere with 'Solar Eclipse'
items.body: The OVO team-up has become one of the biggest songs of the moment, riding into the Hot 100's top 10. It's a hazy, late-night slow-burn that's all over the radio and playlists right now.
items.say: Have you heard 'Solar Eclipse'? Drake and Don Toliver — it's been stuck in my head all week.
